principle_text: When the persuadee indicates limited involvement with charities, avoid focusing solely on their current participation without guiding them toward your specific cause or donation opportunity.
When the persuadee is aware of a charity but has not considered donating, you should introduce the charity and directly ask about their willingness to donate to engage them further.

When the persuadee shares a concern or negative information, avoid responding only with empathy or personal anecdotes without steering the conversation toward the donation goal or increasing willingness to donate.
When the persuadee expresses concern or empathy, you should introduce the charity naturally and with care to encourage recognition and positive engagement.
When the persuadee expresses positive recognition of a charitable organization, you should reinforce its mission and impact to build goodwill and encourage further engagement.
When the persuadee shares a neutral or casual personal experience, avoid responding with equally neutral comments that do not guide the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee responds positively but without connection to the donation goal, avoid shifting to unrelated personal topics that do not advance the charitable cause.
When the persuadee responds with neutral, casual information, avoid continuing unrelated small talk that does not connect to the charitable cause or encourage engagement with the donation appeal.
When the persuadee responds positively to small talk without showing interest in the charitable cause, avoid continuing unrelated casual conversation that does not guide toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee responds positively to casual conversation, you should smoothly transition to introducing the charity to build rapport and set a foundation for donation discussion.
When the persuadee shows openness to donating, you should make a clear and specific request for a small, manageable donation amount to encourage immediate positive engagement.
When a potential donor seeks clarification about how their contribution will be handled, you should provide clear reassurance about the donation process to build trust and encourage commitment.
When a persuadee agrees to donate, avoid generic compliments that do not reinforce or deepen their commitment to the cause.
When the persuadee shares personal background unrelated to the charity, avoid shifting focus to unrelated topics that do not advance the donation conversation.
When the persuadee shows limited knowledge about a charity, avoid assuming familiarity or overwhelming them with details too quickly.
When the persuadee already donates to some charities, avoid only sharing your own generosity without guiding them toward a specific call to action or commitment.
When the persuadee reveals prior charitable giving and openness to helping others, you should acknowledge and build on their generosity to encourage further engagement and donations.
When the persuadee expresses difficulty focusing on multiple social issues, avoid abruptly shifting topics without connecting them to maintain engagement and relevance.
When the persuadee expresses a personal connection or empathy toward the cause, you should acknowledge and build on that connection to deepen engagement and encourage support.
When the persuadee responds with neutral or clarifying questions, avoid focusing solely on personal stories that do not connect to the charitable cause or donation request.
